headline: A new Elon University survey finds most Americans expect AI to destroy more jobs than it creates, even though two-thirds of workers are comfortable using it or would welcome it with training.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a sizeable national survey with clear figures on worker attitudes, but it measures expectations and is published by the surveyors themselves.
importance_line: American workers say they are open to using AI but expect fewer, lower-paid and less meaningful jobs and have little faith that employers or government will help, while employers and policymakers are the audience; these are opinions from 1,158 adults, with a margin of error of 3.4 points, not measured job outcomes.
summary: Elon University's Imagining the Digital Future Center reports from its national survey of 1,158 US adults, fielded by the polling firm SSRS on 20 to 24 August, that 83% expect AI to eliminate more jobs than it creates, 68% expect most jobs to pay too little for a decent lifestyle, and 65% agree that less meaningful work would cost people their sense of purpose and dignity. At the same time, 66% of working adults say they are already comfortable using AI at work or would welcome it with more training, while only 22% of workers are extremely or very confident that their employer would help them if AI affected their jobs.
notes: Full text read; this is the university's own release on its own survey, with a margin of error of 3.4 points. Fieldwork was 20-24 Aug 2026; published 13 Oct 2026.
